criteria.text: Moderate to severe hemophilia B (congenital Factor IX deficiency) (approval criterion 3; FDA indication).
Currently uses Factor IX prophylaxis OR has current or historical life-threatening hemorrhage OR repeated, serious spontaneous bleeding episodes (FDA indications 1-3; approval criterion 3).
Patient is 18 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a hematologist (approval criterion 2).
Factor IX levels ≤2% of normal or <2 IU/dl (approval criterion 4).
Patient has had >150 previous exposure days to Factor IX (approval criterion 5).
No history of Factor IX inhibitors AND a negative screen ≤0.5 Bethesda units performed within two weeks prior to administration (approval criterion 6).
Hepatic ultrasound AND elastography performed prior to administration (approval criterion 7).
No current active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection (denial criterion 2).
No current uncontrolled HIV infection (denial criterion 3).
No evidence of advanced hepatic impairment (denial criterion 4).
No previous gene therapy for hemophilia B (denial criterion 5).

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Hemgenix (etranacogene dezaparvovec-drlb), an AAV vector-based gene therapy for hemophilia B. Version: 1; Original: 1/25/2023; Accepted: 4/21/2023; Effective: 6/1/2023.
Encoded: closed indication, separate clinical eligibility OR paths, approval criteria 1-7 and denial exclusions 2-5. Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria.
Duration (notes only): initial approval 3 months; no reauthorization will be approved.
Quantity (notes only): one infusion per lifetime. HCPCS J3590. No numeric quantity enforcement; max_units is null.
Cautions (notes only): monitor transaminase levels once weekly for three months following administration for possible hepatotoxicity.

Cautions (notes only): patients with preexisting hepatocellular carcinoma risk factors should be monitored regularly for elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and receive abdominal ultrasound screenings for five years following administration.

Remaining gaps: documentation verification, duration, no reauthorization, lifetime quantity enforcement and post-dose monitoring require manual review. Clinical findings, exposure days, testing and imaging are attestations.
PDL status unknown. Evaluate-linked alternative: Beqvez; peer eligibility requires its own criteria review.
